propositions.text: Applicant applied for permanent residence under a COVID-19 health care sector refugee claimants program.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Adejoke Omobolanle Kolawole, applied for permanent residence under a time-limited public policy program for those who made a refugee claim and worked in the health care sector during the COVID-19 pandemic

propositions.text: An IRCC officer refused her application due to inadmissibility under section 42(1) IRPA for having an inadmissible family member.
propositions.quote: An officer at Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada [IRCC] refused her application. The Officer found her ineligible for the Pathway Program due to her inadmissibility under section 42(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act

paragraphs.summary: Applicant applied for permanent residence under a COVID-19 health care refugee claimants program; IRCC officer refused due to inadmissibility under section 42(1) IRPA.

propositions.text: Ms. Kolawole was unaware of her or her husband's inadmissibility found in December 2019 for misrepresentation on a TRV application.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole was surprised by this decision. She did not know she was inadmissible to Canada; nor that in December 2019 her husband was found inadmissible under section 40(1) of the IRPA for misrepresenting on a Temporary Resident Visa application

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kolawole was unaware of her or her husband's inadmissibility found in December 2019 for misrepresentation on a TRV application.

propositions.text: Decision to reject her application is unfair and reasons insufficient due to no notice of spouse's inadmissibility until Officer's decision.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole argues that the decision to reject her application is unfair and the reasons are insufficient because she had no notice of her spouse’s inadmissibility, and therefore her own inadmissibility, until she received the Officer’s decision on her permanent residence application

propositions.text: She had no opportunity to respond to inadmissibility findings.
propositions.quote: She says that this left her with no opportunity to respond

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues rejection was unfair and lacked notice, leaving no opportunity to respond to inadmissibility findings.

propositions.text: There are significant concerns about the soundness of the Officer’s ineligibility decision.
propositions.quote: There are indeed significant concerns regarding the soundness of the Officer’s ineligibility decision

propositions.text: Basis of husband's inadmissibility may not be valid, questioning its use to find applicant inadmissible and ineligible.
propositions.quote: it became apparent that the very basis of Ms. Kolawole’s husband’s inadmissibility may not be valid. This calls into question if it can serve as a basis to find Ms. Kolawole an inadmissible family member and as a consequence ineligible for the Pathway Program

paragraphs.summary: Court finds significant concerns about Officer’s decision and questions validity of husband's inadmissibility as basis for applicant's ineligibility.

propositions.text: Decision relying on inadmissibility determination not in accordance with law cannot stand and must be sent back for redetermination.
propositions.quote: where the decision at issue relies on a determination that the Court has serious concerns is not in accordance with the law, the decision cannot stand and must be sent back for redetermination

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes decision based on questionable inadmissibility must be set aside and remanded for redetermination.

propositions.text: Judicial review is allowed for reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, I allow the judicial review

paragraphs.summary: Court allows the judicial review.

propositions.text: Temporary Public Policy created under section 25.2 IRPA for refugee claimants in health care during COVID-19 pandemic.
propositions.quote: The Temporary public policy to facilitate the granting of permanent residence for certain refugee claimants working in the health care sector during the COVID-19 pandemic (“Temporary Public Policy”) was created by the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration through their public policy power under section 25.2 of the IRPA

propositions.text: Program was time-limited from Dec 14, 2020 to Aug 31, 2021, recognizing refugee claimants' contributions during pandemic.
propositions.quote: The program became operational on December 14, 2020 and ended on August 31, 2021. The government created the Temporary Public Policy to recognize the “extraordinary contribution of refugee claimants working in Canada’s health care sector during the COVID-19 pandemic”

paragraphs.summary: Court explains Temporary Public Policy created under IRPA section 25.2, time-limited, recognizing refugee claimants' health care contributions during COVID-19.

propositions.text: Temporary Public Policy sets eligibility requirements including type, hours, and period of health care work.
propositions.quote: The text of the Temporary Public Policy set out specific eligibility requirements, including the type of health care work that would qualify, as well as guidance on the number of hours of work required and the time period when the work had to have taken place

paragraphs.summary: Temporary Public Policy specifies eligibility requirements on health care work type, hours, and period.

propositions.text: Applicants must not be inadmissible to Canada; exceptions exist for certain non-compliance under section 41(a) IRPA.
propositions.quote: Another requirement was that applicants not be inadmissible to Canada. The Temporary Public Policy provided exceptions to its general bar on inadmissibility. These exceptions recognized that a number of circumstances that result in inadmissibility because of non-compliance with the Act under section 41(a) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: Applicants must not be inadmissible, but exceptions exist for certain non-compliance under section 41(a) IRPA.

propositions.text: Section 22 IRPR exempts refugee claimants with pending claims or recognized refugees from misrepresentation inadmissibility under section 40(1) IRPA.
propositions.quote: Section 22 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227 [IRPR] further exempts refugee claimants whose refugee claims are pending and those recognized as refugees from being found inadmissible because of misrepresentation under section 40(1) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: Section 22 IRPR exempts refugee claimants with pending claims from misrepresentation inadmissibility under section 40(1) IRPA.

propositions.text: Applicant applied on August 3, 2021 with husband and children as dependants; refused September 3, 2021 due to inadmissibility under section 42 IRPA.
propositions.quote: On August 3, 2021, Ms. Kolawole applied for permanent residence through the Pathway Program, including her husband and three minor children as dependants on her application. An Officer at IRCC refused her application on September 3, 2021, finding her ineligible for the program because she was inadmissible under section 42 of the IRPA

propositions.text: Husband found inadmissible in December 2019 for misrepresentation on TRV application filed from Nigeria in November 2018.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole’s inadmissibility was a direct consequence of a December 2019 IRCC decision to find her husband inadmissible for misrepresentation on a TRV that had been filed from Nigeria in November 2018

propositions.text: Applicant alleges she never knew about her or husband's inadmissibility until receiving Officer's decision; family did not receive December 2019 decision addressed to a hotel in North York.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole alleges on this application that she never knew about her or her husband’s inadmissibility until receiving the Officer’s decision. Ms. Kolawole claims that her family did not receive the IRCC’s December 2019 decision that was addressed to a hotel in North York, Ontario

paragraphs.summary: Applicant applied with family; refused due to husband's 2019 inadmissibility; applicant alleges no prior knowledge or receipt of decision.

propositions.text: Applicant and family made refugee claims in August 2019 at Roxham Road; claims pending at time of application.
propositions.quote: In August 2019, Ms. Kolawole, her husband, and her children entered Canada from the United States through the Roxham Road crossing, and immediately made refugee claims. At the time Ms. Kolawole applied for the Pathway Program, all their refugee claims remained pending before the Immigration and Refugee Board

paragraphs.summary: Applicant and family made refugee claims in August 2019 at Roxham Road; claims pending at application time.

propositions.text: Applicant framed arguments on procedural fairness and notice; court finds it unnecessary to address duty to notify.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole primarily framed her arguments around procedural fairness and notice. I have found it unnecessary to address the issue of whether the Officer had a duty to notify Ms. Kolawole of her potential inadmissibility in these circumstances

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argued procedural fairness and notice; court declines to address duty to notify issue.

propositions.text: Court has serious concerns about validity of inadmissibility decision leading to applicant's ineligibility; this is determinative issue.
propositions.quote: I have serious concerns about the validity of the inadmissibility decision that led to Ms. Kolawole being found to be inadmissible, and as a consequence, ineligible for the Pathway Program. I find this to be the determinative issue

paragraphs.summary: Court finds serious concerns about inadmissibility decision's validity, which is the determinative issue.

propositions.text: Standard of review is reasonableness per Vavilov: whether rejection is reasonable given serious concerns about basis of inadmissibility.
propositions.quote: As this issue is about the substantive merits of the decision, I have considered it on a reasonableness standard (Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov] at para 25), namely: whether it is reasonable to allow the rejection of Ms. Kolawole’s application to stand when, apparent on the face of the record before the Officer, there are serious concerns that the very basis on which she was found ineligible may not be valid

paragraphs.summary: Court applies reasonableness standard per Vavilov to assess if rejection is reasonable given serious concerns about inadmissibility basis.

propositions.text: Misrepresentation inadmissibility decision date (Dec 2, 2019) postdates refugee claim date (Aug 26, 2019); family were refugee claimants when inadmissibility found.
propositions.quote: There are two critical dates: the date of the inadmissibility decision on Mr. Kolawole’s TRV application (December 2, 2019), and the date that Ms. Kolawole and her family made refugee claims (August 26, 2019). From these two undisputed dates, it is clear that at the time that the misrepresentation finding was made under section 40(1)(a) of the IRPA, the family, including Ms. Kolawole’s husband, were already in Canada as refugee claimants

paragraphs.summary: Court finds misrepresentation inadmissibility decision postdates refugee claim; family were refugee claimants when inadmissibility found.

propositions.text: Section 22 IRPR exempts refugee claimants with pending claims from misrepresentation inadmissibility under section 40(1)(a) IRPA.
propositions.quote: Section 22 of the IRPR reads as follows: Persons who have claimed refugee protection, if disposition of the claim is pending, and protected persons within the meaning of subsection 95(2) of the Act are exempted from the application of paragraph 40(1)(a) of the Act

propositions.text: Misrepresentation inadmissibility finding appears contrary to section 22 IRPR exemption.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the misrepresentation inadmissibility finding appears to be contrary to section 22 of the IRPR

paragraphs.summary: Court finds misrepresentation inadmissibility appears contrary to section 22 IRPR exemption for refugee claimants with pending claims.

propositions.text: This raises serious concern whether inadmissibility finding can be relied on to find applicant inadmissible and ineligible for Pathway Program.
propositions.quote: This is a serious concern, calling into whether this foundational inadmissibility determination — the misrepresentation inadmissibility finding that appears to have been made contrary to the law — can be relied upon to find Ms. Kolawole inadmissible and ineligible for the Pathway Program

propositions.text: Almrei v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) supports that invalid inadmissibility cannot be basis for ineligibility.
propositions.quote: (Almrei v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2011 FC 554 at para 46)

paragraphs.summary: Court seriously questions if invalid inadmissibility can support applicant's ineligibility, citing Almrei precedent.

propositions.text: Applicant's refusal lacked consideration of potential invalidity; decision not reasonable given serious concerns on record.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole’s application was refused without any consideration of this potential invalidity. I do not find the ineligibility decision can be upheld as reasonable when, apparent on the face of the record before the Officer, there are serious concerns that the very basis for Ms. Kolawole’s inadmissibility and consequential ineligibility for the Pathway Program may not be in accordance with the law

propositions.text: Vavilov para 101 supports that decision untenable if not in accordance with relevant factual and legal constraints.
propositions.quote: In these circumstances, the decision is untenable in light of the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on it (Vavilov at para 101)

paragraphs.summary: Court finds refusal unreasonable for ignoring potential invalidity, citing Vavilov that decision is untenable if not legally sound.

propositions.text: Respondent's arguments at hearing focused on applicant's failure to challenge inadmissibility and futility of redetermination.
propositions.quote: The Respondent’s arguments focused on two issues: i) the Applicant and her family’s failure to challenge the misrepresentation inadmissibility decision when they learned of it; and ii) the futility of sending the matter back for redetermination

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argued applicant failed to challenge inadmissibility and redetermination would be futile.

propositions.text: The real issue is the husband's misrepresentation inadmissibility decision, not before the court
propositions.quote: The Respondent characterized the real issue as being one that was not before me — the husband’s misrepresentation inadmissibility decision

propositions.text: Ms. Kolawole's ineligibility flows from her husband's inadmissibility decision
propositions.quote: the decision to find Ms. Kolawole ineligible simply flowed from that decision

propositions.text: The problem is the husband's failure to challenge the inadmissibility determination
propositions.quote: The Respondent argued that the real problem lay in the Applicant’s husband failing to challenge the misrepresentation inadmissibility determination

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues the real issue is the husband's inadmissibility decision and failure to challenge it, which caused Ms. Kolawole's ineligibility.

propositions.text: Husband's inadmissibility is the foundation of Ms. Kolawole's ineligibility
propositions.quote: I agree that her husband’s inadmissibility is the foundation upon which Ms. Kolawole’s ineligibility is based

propositions.text: The real concern is the rejection of Ms. Kolawole's permanent residence application, which is before the court
propositions.quote: the question of central and immediate importance is the rejection of her permanent residence application

propositions.text: The husband's TRV inadmissibility finding is irrelevant to the family now but was relied on to find Ms. Kolawole inadmissible
propositions.quote: The TRV application resulting in Mr. Kolawole’s inadmissibility finding has long ago become irrelevant to this family... relied upon to find Ms. Kolawole inadmissible

propositions.text: The inadmissibility finding is core to Ms. Kolawole's judicial review challenge and properly before the court
propositions.quote: The reliance on that inadmissibility finding is core to her challenge on judicial review and is appropriately before me

paragraphs.summary: Court finds husband's inadmissibility underpins Ms. Kolawole's rejection, which is the central issue before the court.

propositions.text: Judicial review of husband's inadmissibility was not pursued because family only learned of it in Sept 2021
propositions.quote: Ms. Kolawole’s counsel explained that a judicial review... had not been pursued because the family only learned of the decision in September 2021

propositions.text: Husband could have challenged the decision in Sept 2021 or requested extension to file challenge
propositions.quote: The Respondent argued that Mr. Kolawole could have challenged the decision in September 2021... and/or have requested an extension of time

paragraphs.summary: Applicant says family only learned of inadmissibility in 2021; Respondent says husband could have challenged then or sought extension.

propositions.text: Potential avenues existed to challenge husband's inadmissibility
propositions.quote: there may have been potential avenues that the Applicant and her family could have pursued

propositions.text: Failure to challenge is not sufficient to ignore concern about inadmissibility decision's legality
propositions.quote: I do not... view their failure to do so to be a sufficient basis for the Court to ignore its concern

propositions.text: Rejection consequences are severe and reapplication is impossible as program ended
propositions.quote: The consequences of a rejection are severe for Ms. Kolawole and her family. Ms. Kolawole cannot reapply... because the program is no longer operational

paragraphs.summary: Court finds failure to challenge inadmissibility doesn't override concern about its legality; rejection consequences are severe and reapplication impossible.

propositions.text: No remedy possible on redetermination as officer must find inadmissibility remains unchallenged
propositions.quote: even if the Court were to send the matter back... officer’s hands would be tied

propositions.text: Sending matter back without directions likely won't address judicial review concerns
propositions.quote: sending the matter back with no further directions... may likely result in the key concern... not being addressed

propositions.text: Unusual circumstances require a creative remedy to prevent injustice
propositions.quote: this unusual circumstance calls for a creative remedy in order to prevent a potential injustice

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says no remedy on redetermination; court agrees without directions but orders creative remedy to prevent injustice.

propositions.text: Matter sent back for redetermination with directions to address legal validity of husband's inadmissibility
propositions.quote: I am ordering the matter be sent back to be redetermined with specific directions that address the legal validity concern

propositions.text: Officer must not finalize until Applicant and family can address potential invalidity of husband's inadmissibility
propositions.quote: The Officer is directed to not finally determine this matter until the Applicant and her family have had an opportunity to address

propositions.text: Judicial review granted; September 3, 2021 decision quashed; matter sent to different officer for redetermination
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is granted;... The September 3, 2021 decision is quashed and the matter is sent back

propositions.text: Officer must notify Applicant, seek husband's consent to reopen inadmissibility finding, and hold application in abeyance
propositions.quote: The officer redetermining the application must notify the Applicant... ask for confirmation of Mr. Kolawole’s consent... application must be held in abeyance

propositions.text: If husband consents, officer must seek to reopen inadmissibility and provide court's judgment to IRCC officer
propositions.quote: If Mr. Kolawole provides his consent, the officer must seek to have the December 2, 2019 inadmissibility finding re-opened

propositions.text: If husband does not consent, officer must give Applicant 60 days for further submissions
propositions.quote: If Mr. Kolawole does not provide his consent, the officer must provide the Applicant with 60 days to provide any further submissions

propositions.text: Parties may apply for clarification if difficulties arise during redetermination
propositions.quote: The parties remain at liberty to apply to me... for clarification if difficulties arise with implementation

paragraphs.summary: Court orders redetermination with directions, including seeking husband's consent to reopen inadmissibility, holding application in abeyance, and allowing submissions.
